page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.8xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, and network connectivity is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

The underlying AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which accelerate vector and neural network operations. Cryptographic tasks benefit from hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions. The architecture also includes integer and bit manipulation features such as BMI2, ADX, and FMA, alongside security mitigations like IBRS and SSBD.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.g8a.8xlarge demonstrates strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, such as the Geekbench multi-core score, also ranks in the top 25%, while stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores fall within the middle 50%. Memory performance is strong, as evidenced by a Passmark memory score in the top 25%. Cryptographic operations are highly efficient, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring in the top 25%.

The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-intensive workloads. However, the balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and strong single-core capabilities make this instance suitable for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, software compilation, text processing, and database operations.
